question: Compare the portfolio to public comps
html:
The public comps place BSP's portfolio companies in three economic groups: high-growth, thin-margin trades; services businesses valued on productivity per head; and ex-growth agencies. Without portfolio company financials in the context, these are directional reference points, not a scored comparison.

How the comps sort

  • Construction and trades (CET, Punctual Pros): Electrical and MEP comps grew revenue 16.8% a year from FY2023 to FY2025, versus 8.4% for residential. Commercial electrical earns a median 6.4% operating margin. Only FIX (14.4%), IESC (11.4%) and EME (10.1%) reach 10% or more (Public comparables).
  • People-based services (Frontline): Offshore BPO earns 12-15% operating margins at $18k-$35k revenue per employee. Onshore professional services such as CBIZ ($290k) and Kyndryl ($210k) earn only 3-9% (Public comparables).
  • Agencies (BPI): These are ex-growth. The median growth rate is +0.3%, and WPP fell 8.1% in GBP (Public comparables).

Portfolio versus benchmarks

Portfolio companyComp readImplication
Punctual ProsResidential median: 13.6% growth, 14.4% operating margin, about $401k revenue per employeeMid-teens EBITDA is the mature target. Pure residential installers grew only 1-1.5%
CETElectrical median growth 16.9%; margins thinValue comes from service and mission-critical mix, not price
FrontlineOnshore services earn 3-9%Expect CBIZ-like economics unless offshore leverage is added
BPIMedian agency growth +0.3%Growth premium has to come from products such as monitoring

Where premiums come from

  • Buyers pay for recurring, visible earnings. PKF puts project-heavy HVAC firms at 5-6x EBITDA and repeatable-service firms at 10x+. Capstone/IMAP show a typical 6.8x versus a premium 9.8x (ServiceOS evidence).
  • The estimated tech-enabled premium is 1.0-2.5 turns for Punctual Pros and 0.5-1.5 turns each for CET and Frontline (est.). Scale explains most 17-20x roll-up prints (ServiceOS evidence).
  • For Thomas Scientific, the comps support an EBITDA case rather than a multiple premium. Avantor runs about 80% digital transactions (ServiceOS evidence).
  • The AI-agent program estimates about $12.7M of annual run-rate EBITDA-equivalent value. That figure rests on analyst assumptions that still need system-of-record volumes (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Caveats and data gaps

  • Comp figures are GAAP as reported. Comp EBITDA is operating income plus D&A, not Adjusted EBITDA (Public comparables).
  • The context does not contain revenue, margin or headcount-productivity figures for the portfolio companies. Placing each company inside its comp range requires trailing twelve-month revenue, adjusted EBITDA and current headcount. Frontline headcount alone (about 1,100 in Jan 2026, per the BSP firm profile) is not enough to compute revenue per employee.
  • Fair Harbor's comp set and benchmarks are not in the extract.

Next actions

  1. Pull trailing twelve-month revenue, EBITDA and headcount for each portfolio company. Compute margin and revenue per employee against the comp medians.
  2. Size Punctual Pros' recurring and membership revenue share. That share is the driver behind the 10x+ service multiples.
  3. Measure CET's service and mission-critical revenue mix against FIX, IESC and EME.
  4. Model Frontline's onshore versus offshore delivery mix to test the CBIZ-like margin ceiling (est.).
